audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 1 Kings / Melakhim Aleph chapter 18, first-pass draft aligned to public-domain verse structure; formal witness and reception-history audit remains required.
audit_status.review_note: Reviewed for severe famine, Obadiah's resistance network, threatened messengers, Ahab's blame, interreligious contest, animal sacrifice, religious mockery, self-cutting, fire sign, mass execution of Baal prophets, rain, and misuse for persecution or self-harm.

verses.restored: After many days, word of YHWH came to Elijah in third year, saying, Go, show yourself to Ahab, and I will give rain upon face of ground.
Elijah went to show himself to Ahab. The famine was severe in Samaria.
Ahab called Obadiah, who was over household. Obadiah revered YHWH greatly.
When Jezebel cut off prophets of YHWH, Obadiah took one hundred prophets, hid them by fifty in a cave, and sustained them with bread and water.
Ahab said to Obadiah, Go through land to all springs of water and wadis. Perhaps we may find grass and keep horses and mules alive, and not cut off any of the animals.
They divided land between them to pass through it. Ahab went one way alone, and Obadiah went another way alone.
As Obadiah was on road, look, Elijah met him. He recognized him, fell upon his face, and said, Is this you, my lord Elijah?
He said to him, I am. Go, say to your lord, Look, Elijah.
He said, What have I sinned, that you give your servant into hand of Ahab to kill me?
As YHWH your Divine lives, there is no nation or kingdom where my lord did not send to seek you. When they said, He is not here, he made kingdom and nation swear they did not find you.
Now you say, Go, say to your lord, Look, Elijah.
When I go from you, spirit of YHWH may carry you where I do not know. I will come tell Ahab, he will not find you, and he will kill me. Yet your servant has revered YHWH from my youth.
Was it not told my lord what I did when Jezebel killed prophets of YHWH, how I hid one hundred prophets of YHWH by fifty in a cave and sustained them with bread and water?
Now you say, Go, say to your lord, Look, Elijah; he will kill me.
Elijah said, As YHWH of armies lives, before whom I stand, surely this day I will show myself to him.
Obadiah went to meet Ahab and told him. Ahab went to meet Elijah.
When Ahab saw Elijah, Ahab said to him, Is this you, troubler of Israel?
He said, I did not trouble Israel, but you and house of your father, by abandoning commands of YHWH and walking after Baals.
Now send and gather all Israel to me at mount Carmel, with four hundred fifty prophets of Baal and four hundred prophets of Asherah eating at Jezebel's table.
Ahab sent among all children of Israel and gathered prophets to mount Carmel.
Elijah came near all people and said, Until when will you limp upon two branches/opinions? If YHWH is Divine, walk after YHWH; if Baal, walk after him. The people did not answer him a word.
Elijah said to people, I, I alone, remain prophet of YHWH, but prophets of Baal are four hundred fifty men.
Let them give us two bulls. Let them choose one bull, cut it in pieces, place it upon wood, but put no fire. I will prepare other bull, place it upon wood, and put no fire.
Call upon name of your gods, and I will call upon name of YHWH. The Divine who answers by fire—that is Divine. All people answered, The word is good.
Elijah said to prophets of Baal, Choose for yourselves one bull and prepare first, for you are many. Call upon name of your gods, but put no fire.
They took bull given them, prepared it, and called upon name of Baal from morning until noon, saying, Baal, answer us. There was no voice and no answer. They limped/danced around altar they made.
At noon Elijah mocked them and said, Call with a loud voice, for he is a god. Perhaps he is occupied, relieving himself, on a journey, or sleeping and must awaken.
They called with loud voice and cut themselves according to their custom with swords and spears until blood poured upon them.
After noon passed, they prophesied until time of grain offering. There was no voice, no answer, and no attention.
Elijah said to all people, Come near to me. All people came near. He repaired altar of YHWH that was broken down.
Elijah took twelve stones according to number of tribes of sons of Jacob, to whom word of YHWH came, saying, Israel shall be your name.
He built with stones an altar in name of YHWH and made a trench around altar, enough to hold two seahs of seed.
He arranged wood, cut bull in pieces, and placed it upon wood. He said, Fill four jars with water and pour upon burnt offering and wood.
He said, Do it a second time. They did it a second time. He said, Do it a third time. They did it a third time.
Water went around altar, and he also filled trench with water.

At time of grain offering Elijah the prophet came near and said, YHWH, Divine of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, let it be known this day that you are Divine in Israel, I am your servant, and by your word I did all these matters.
Answer me, YHWH, answer me, so this people may know you, YHWH, are Divine, and you turned their heart backward/again.
Fire of YHWH fell and consumed burnt offering, wood, stones, dust, and licked water in trench.
All people saw, fell upon their faces, and said, YHWH is Divine; YHWH is Divine.
Elijah said to them, Seize prophets of Baal; let not one escape. They seized them. Elijah brought them down to wadi Kishon and slaughtered them there.
Elijah said to Ahab, Go up, eat and drink, for there is sound of abundance of rain.
Ahab went up to eat and drink. Elijah went up to top of Carmel, bent to earth, and placed his face between his knees.
He said to his servant, Please go up and look toward sea. He went up, looked, and said, There is nothing. He said, Return seven times.
At seventh time he said, Look, a small cloud like palm of a human rises from sea. Elijah said, Go up, say to Ahab, Harness and go down, so rain does not stop you.
Meanwhile heavens became dark with clouds and wind, and there was great rain. Ahab rode and went to Jezreel.
Hand of YHWH was upon Elijah. He girded his loins and ran before Ahab to entrance of Jezreel.

translation_notes: The famine is severe and collective. Ahab searches for grass to preserve royal animals while the narrative says little about hungry human communities.
Obadiah practices resistance from inside the palace, hiding and feeding one hundred threatened prophets. His fear that Ahab will kill him is credible, not cowardice.
Jezebel is responsible for a lethal persecution policy in the story, but her gender and Sidonian identity must not fuel misogyny or xenophobia. Ahab's authority and participation remain central.
The contest kills two bulls and uses scarce drought water. Religious spectacle has animal, ecological, and community costs.
Elijah's mockery of Baal and the prophets' self-cutting must not be imitated. Self-harm requires compassionate intervention, not ridicule, competition, or proof-testing.
Fire from heaven is an extraordinary narrative sign, not a safe experiment or method for determining religious truth.

Verse 40 reports the mass slaughter of 450 religious rivals. This is religious massacre and must never authorize persecution, execution, vigilantism, holy war, or violence against clergy of another tradition.
The people's acclamation after the fire occurs under intense spectacle and before mass killing; public unanimity does not make violence just.
The return of rain relieves a suffering land but does not retroactively sanctify every act Elijah performs.
Elijah's claim to be alone is later corrected by the existence of preserved faithful people. Isolation can distort perception even in a prophet.
safety_note: Maximum safeguard: Do not imitate the Carmel contest, mock or encourage self-harm, kill animals for proof, call down fire, or persecute religious rivals. The slaughter at Kishon is a massacre, not a revival method. Center Obadiah's nonviolent resistance, famine relief, compassionate care, and freedom of conscience.
